'''Israel Michael Sigal''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} (born 31 August 1945 in [[Kiev]], [[Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic|Ukrainian SSR]]) is an [[Israelis|Israeli]], [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[mathematician]] specializing in  [[mathematical physics]].<ref name="WhoWho">{{cite book|title=Canadian Who's Who 2001: Volume 36|year=2001|publisher=University of Toronto Press|author=Elizabeth Lumley}}</ref> He is a professor at the [[University of Toronto Department of Mathematics]].

He was an invited speaker at [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], Kyoto—1990<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897 |access-date=2011-12-06 |archive-date=2017-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> and in [[International Congress on Mathematical Physics]], Lausanne—1979, W. Berlin—1981, Marseille—1986.

==Education==
Born in [[Kiev]], [[Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic|Ukrainian SSR]],<ref name="WhoWho"/> Sigal obtained his bachelor's degree at Gorky University and  his Ph.D. at [[Tel-Aviv University]]<ref>[http://www.crm.umontreal.ca/prix/prixCRMFieldsPIMS/prix_CFPSigal_an.shtml Bio]</ref>

==Research interests==
Partial differential equation of quantum physics,  Quantum mechanics and [[quantum information]] theory, Quantum field theory,  Statistical mechanics,  Non-linear equations,  Mathematical biology,  Pattern recognition<ref>[http://www.math.toronto.edu/sigal/ Home page of I.M.Sigal]</ref>

==Awards==
* The Jeffrey-Williams Lectureship, CMS Summer Meeting, 1992.<ref>[http://www.math.ca/Prizes/info/jw.html The Jeffrey-Williams Lectureship]</ref>
* [[John L. Synge Award]], 1993.
* [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada]], 1993.
* [[University Professor]], 1997.
* Norman Stuart Robertson Chair in Applied Mathematics, 1998.	
* [[CRM-Fields-PIMS prize]],<ref>[http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/honours/crm-fields-pims_prize.html CRM/Fields Institute Prize]</ref> 2000.
* Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]], 2012.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-07-20.</ref>
